newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Laker sues BA over Gatwick slots.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Laker sues BA over Gatwick slots.

text.p: Laker Airways, the cut-price airline headed by maverick business tycoon Sir Freddy Laker, on Thursday announced it would sue British Airways over landing and take-off slots at Gatwick Airport, south of London.
Laker Airways claims British Airways is violating U.S. antitrust laws, saying the UK flag carrier is denying Laker fair competition on the London-Miaimi route.
Laker Airways said it filed a suit against British Airways today in the Federal Court in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, Laker's home base.
Laker charges British Airways (BA) controls Gatwick slots, claiming the slot co-ordinator, Airport Co-ordination Ltd, is being controlled by BA.
"Under EU (European Union)regulations the slot co-ordinator must be neutral. This is a farce," Freddie Laker said in a statement.
BA rejected Laker's claims and said it was asking the airline to explain its allegations.

"BA and its subsidiaries hold only 30 percent of the slots at Gatwick -- granted under the law regulating slots in England. That is a small percentage at a home-based airport in this industry," a spokesman for the British flag carrier said.
"If Laker wants slots, it is free to apply for them under the slot allocation regulations which give preferences to new entrants," the company added.
